package_info.package_name: Magecart credit card skimmer (First Aid Beauty site)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (site infection, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The Magecart skimmer is malicious because it is a heavily obfuscated and encrypted JavaScript code injected into a legitimate e-commerce website, designed to steal credit card information from users during checkout. It specifically targets US victims on Windows systems, exfiltrating sensitive payment data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in checkout/payment page of First Aid Beauty site

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form submission, collects credit card data from the DOM, and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in exfiltration of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it is obfuscated, executes in the context of a payment form, and exfiltrates sensitive user data to an external domain not associated with the legitimate business.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce site JavaScript should not collect and transmit credit card data to unknown third-party domains, especially in an obfuscated/encrypted manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processors may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and with transparent code.
key_indicators: Access to payment form fields (credit card number, etc.)
Network requests to untrusted, hardcoded external domains
Execution only for specific geolocations (US) and OS (Windows)

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the checkout/payment page of the First Aid Beauty site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in the browser of site visitors.

attack_chain.action: When a user submits the payment form, the skimmer code collects credit card data from the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of sensitive data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected credit card data is sent via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of payment information to the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript accessing payment form fields
JavaScript sending payment data to external, non-payment domains
Runtime DOM scraping of sensitive fields (credit card, CVV, etc.)
file_indicators: Injected or appended JavaScript in checkout/payment page
Unusual <script> tags or inline event handlers not present in legitimate site code
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the merchant (e.g., malicious-domain.com/collect)
Outbound traffic containing credit card patterns from client browsers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor e-commerce site pages for unauthorized or obfuscated JavaScript, especially code that accesses payment form fields and sends data to unknown external domains. Use web application firewalls to block suspicious outbound requests, and regularly audit site code for unauthorized changes. Network monitoring for POST requests containing credit card data to non-payment domains is also effective.
